# Goldrush (03, engineer) — BAD-002

## Brief
Build guest mode: sign-in becomes optional in the web tree, which means iOS and my.badtakes.io alike. A signed-out user can use everything that runs on the device, and sign-in gates only catalog downloads and collab. Add the per-entry guest allowance to the hosted catalog, hide the public collab list on iOS, and bring the privacy policy, the runbook and the design note in line.

The spec is § 1.6 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-ios-app-review-guest-mode-design.md (Kennebec's research, already in the worktree). Read all of § 1, and § 4.2 and § 4.3. Eric's decisions, which settle § 1.7:
- Guest mode applies everywhere the web tree runs: iOS and the browser. The desktop app (renderer/, main.js) keeps its sign-in gate unchanged.
- The empty-library remedy is B: an `anonymous` mark on individual catalog index entries. A guest can download and install only marked entries; every other entry, and collab, asks for sign-in with an explanation first. No per-device install counter. Which scenes get marked is Eric's call and is not in this change: build the field, carry it through src/showcase.js's entry trimming and the `npm run showcase` publish CLI (a flag at publish time), and mark an entry in the local catalog that `npm run web:fixtures` generates, so it can be tested.
- The public collab list is hidden on iOS (Native.isNative()), so rooms are joined by code only. The browser keeps the list.
- Settings gains a Sign in row for guests, and privacy-policy and contact links for everyone (§ 4.3; the store sheet's link is hidden on iOS now).

Do:
- Run `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` first if the worktree lacks node_modules.
- Implement § 1.6's properties and risks 2 to 4 of § 1.5. Guests get a Catalog treatment that explains before it gates (never a silent redirect to sign-in), and gate copy that says what an account is for ("Sign in for the Catalog and Collabs", not "Sign in to start dubbing"). Sign-in is reached only from the gated doors and Settings, never from boot, a timer or a view change, and signing in from a door returns the user to that door. The empty-library state names both ways in. No endpoint is called without a token, and Report keeps "no token, no row".
- The ads and plan removal just landed on this branch (body.no-plans, test/ios-no-plans.test.js). Keep it intact.
- Reword the iOS paragraph of site/privacy.html: no ads, no tracking and no store subscriptions in the iOS app at present, and nothing collected from a guest who never signs in. Keep the text that is true of the desktop and the web, and update the "last updated" date.
- Remove BT_ADMOB_TESTING from .github/workflows/mobile.yml.
- Update docs/MOBILE-STORES.md's sign-in, reviewer-account and review-note parts (§ A1, § A3, § B8 and the device pass in § C) for guest mode. In the design note, record the decisions above in § 1.7, and resolve § 5's brackets that these decisions settle (remedy B, public list hidden on iOS). Leave brackets that need values only Eric has, such as the build number, REVIEWER_CODE, the sample-file URL and the catalog content basis. Update web/CLAUDE.md and mobile/CLAUDE.md where they say the web app is gated behind sign-in from the first paint.
- Pin it with tests: guest reachability of each on-device function, the gated doors, the anonymous field through src/showcase.js and the publish CLI, the public list hidden on native, no network call without a token.

Verify per the repo's implementing-changes skill: `npm test`. Drive the guest flow in the browser (`npm run web` with the local catalog; the memory note web-verification-environment-tips covers the Browser pane's microphone and IndexedDB quirks): a fresh profile opens on the library with no sign-in, the marked catalog entry installs, an unmarked entry explains and then asks for sign-in, a file-added scene runs table read, booth and screening, and export works. Then `npm run mobile:check`, and a fresh-install simulator run of the same guest path with screenshots under the scratchpad. If src/ changes reach the desktop, run the smoke leg that covers them.

The local Supabase stack is currently DOWN and serves every worktree. Never stop, start or restart it, and never run a podman command that changes state (podman ps is fine). The guest flow needs no stack. If the stack is up when you get there, also verify signing in from a gated door and the hidden public list on iOS. If it is down, record those checks as owed in your result, not as passed.
